name: @arcane-spark/ubel-node
description: Software supply-chain and source-code security for Node.js. SCA: resolves dependencies, scans via OSV.dev and NVD, annotates findings with heuristic reachability and exploit intelligence (CISA KEV + FIRST EPSS), suggests per-package upgrade paths, and writes a plain-language executive summary (SBOM/CycloneDX + SARIF reporting). Firewall: gates npm/pnpm/bun installs behind a lockfile-only dry-run scan before anything reaches node_modules, with atomic revert and TOCTOU protection; also gates pip/uv/pipx installs behind a dry-run resolution (`pip install --dry-run` / `uv pip install --dry-run`), Poetry installs behind `poetry add --lock` resolved in a scratch copy of the project (then `poetry install --no-root` from precisely the scanned pyproject.toml + poetry.lock, source distributions refused), conda installs behind `conda create --dry-run --json` against a scratch prefix (then an exact-pinned `--no-deps` install of precisely the scanned set), Cargo (Rust) installs behind `cargo add` + `cargo update --workspace` resolved in a scratch copy of the project (then `cargo fetch --locked` of precisely the scanned lockfile), and apt/dnf/yum installs (one dedicated binary per package manager) behind each one's own native dry-run, in both cases before anything is actually installed (no lockfile concept there, so no revert/TOCTOU step — a rejected scan simply never runs the real install). Yarn, Bundler, Go, .NET, Dart, Flutter and SwiftPM have no dry-run UBEL can safely drive, so they are `check`-only: the lockfile must already exist and `check` scans exactly what it pins (no manifest, no package-manager binary needed); there is no `install` mode. Also includes an AI-powered SAST engine (scan → verify → taint-trace) for source-level vulnerability detection, a separate malicious-code/backdoor scanner (both with JSON, HTML, and SARIF reporting), and a cloud misconfiguration scanner for AWS/GCP/Azure — public exposure, IAM, encryption, and audit-logging posture via each provider's own read-only API, with JSON and HTML reporting; and an EASM module that passively fingerprints a domain/URL's exposed software over HTTP and checks it against OSV.dev/NVD, plus a fixed set of misconfiguration checks (exposed .env/.git/docker-compose files, Spring Boot Actuator env and Swagger/OpenAPI endpoints, TLS/certificate weaknesses, missing security headers and cookie flags, risky HTTP methods, CORS misconfiguration, and SPF/DMARC/DKIM email-authentication gaps), with JSON and HTML reporting. The EASM module ships as four binaries: `ubel-url` scans hosts you already know, `ubel-domain` discovers a domain's subdomains from Certificate Transparency logs (crt.sh) first and scans all of them in one run, `ubel-host` resolves one or more IPs/domains to their distinct IPs (exactly the way `ubel-easm` handles crt.sh hostnames), port-scans each, probes every open port for HTTP(S), and scans whatever answers, and `ubel-easm` combines the two — discovering a domain's subdomains, resolving them to their distinct IP addresses, then port-scanning and fingerprinting every one of those IPs and mapping the combined results against OSV/NVD/wpvulnerability.net in a single run — all four for authorized use only, against infrastructure you own. A mobile app scanner (`ubel-mobile`) statically analyses an Android .apk / .aab (and split bundles .xapk / .apks / .apkm) or iOS .ipa — hardcoded secrets, insecure storage and data handling, and misconfigurations (manifest/Info.plist, network security config/ATS, signing, TLS-validation bypasses, WebView settings, per-ABI native-library hardening), React Native / Flutter / Unity / Xamarin app code, packer and obfuscator detection, a behavior inventory with the remote hosts the app names, and known-vulnerable components bundled in its native libraries (version banners checked against NVD, Go modules and Rust crates against OSV.dev), mapped to OWASP MASVS — using only Node built-ins (no third-party libraries, no external binaries), with JSON and HTML reporting; an opt-in `--online` mode adds three read-only checks against hosts the app itself names (assetlinks.json, an open Firebase Realtime Database, Firebase Remote Config). A native binary scanner (`ubel-binary`) does the same for a single ELF, Mach-O (thin or fat) or PE executable or library — build hardening (PIE, NX, RELRO, canary, FORTIFY, hardened runtime, ASLR/DEP/CFG …), risky imports, a behavior inventory with call sites, hardcoded secrets, remote hosts, and known-vulnerable components (C/C++ version banners → NVD; Go modules, Rust crates and the npm / Python packages of pkg, Node SEA, Bun and PyInstaller applications → OSV.dev) — nothing is executed or loaded, and a failed lookup is reported as an incomplete analysis (exit 3), never as clean. A package scanner (`ubel-package <name> <version> <ecosystem> [--registry <url>]`) downloads one dependency release from its registry (npm, PyPI, crates.io, Go, RubyGems, NuGet, Packagist, pub.dev) and statically analyses the archive — install / build-time scripts and what they do, packages installed by those scripts, the pin class of every dependency, remote hosts, a behavior inventory, hardcoded secrets, native binaries inside the package, archive integrity, and known-vulnerable or known-malicious versions (OSV.dev) — without installing, building or running anything, and a failed lookup is an incomplete analysis (exit 3), never a clean result.
author: Ala Bouali <ala.bouali.1997@gmail.com>
